hafsa: following up from the RFC review - i wired a prototype that combines an ownership-fence token, a tiny LRU rehydrate buffer, and a per-tenant evict throttle. sketch + observations below. goals: avoid R/W violations during demote/evict, reduce coordinated demotes, and keep origin hits bounded for low-signal tenants.

colin: nice, can you outline the ownership-fence token semantics? is it different from leased_epoch checks we've used?

hafsa: yes, similar idea but explicit token from ownership service that proves the prefix state is stable for a short window. semantic: token(ttl_ms, seq_token). runtime caches token and only allows demote/evict if cached_token.valid() && cached_token.seq_token == current_seq. compared to epoch checks this is explicit and easier to reason about in tests. pseudocode: 

hafsa: ```
# ownership token refresher (async)
on_ownership_update(prefix, seq_token, stable_until_ms):
  cache[prefix] = OwnershipToken(seq_token, stable_until_ms)

# demote decision (hot path)
for prefix in active_prefixes:
  token = cache.get(prefix)
  if not token or token.stable_until < now:
    block_demote(prefix, reason='no_token')
    continue
  if prefix.last_write_ms + write_pin_ttl > now:
    block_demote(prefix, reason='recent_write')
    continue
  prob = compute_prob(prefix)
  if rand() < prob:
    attempt_soft_demote(prefix, token.seq_token)
```

grace: how does the LRU rehydrate buffer fit? is it per-node? global?

hafsa: per-node small LRU of recently-demoted prefixes with metadata to allow immediate local rehydrate without origin for a short ttl (rehydrate_ttl). idea: if a read misses shortly after our demote, we can rehydrate from a peer or staged copy inside node (if available) and avoid origin. it's not a full cache, just a fast absorb for flaps. size ~ 256 entries default.

mike: curious about correctness—what if write occurs right after demote and before rehydrate? we must keep read-after-write.

hafsa: invariant: demote only when ownership token proves stability AND last_write_age > write_pin_ttl. if a write happens concurrently, the ownership service must issue a new seq_token and token.stable_until moves forward; our cached token will expire so we won't demote. also rehydrate only serves GETs; writes always go to origin and will bump last_write_ts so future demotes are blocked.

colin: replication lag of ownership tokens could bite us. what's the safety margin?

hafsa: we add two safeguards: 1) token.stable_until has a small safety_margin baked in by ownership service (it only marks stable after commit replication plus margin). 2) runtime requires token.age_ms > min_token_age_ms (e.g., 200ms) to ensure we don't act on freshly observed tokens that might be transient.

grace: per-tenant throttle—how enforced?

hafsa: tenant_budget is expressed as allowed_evictions_per_minute normalized by tenant size. adjudicator tracks evict_count windowed and scales down prob if near budget. small tenants get conservative defaults (lower budget). pseudocode snippet: 

hafsa: ```
allowed = tenant_budget[tenant]
if evict_window.count(tenant) >= allowed:
  prob = prob * downscale_factor
```

mike: i like the tests we should add. propose three categories: unit checks for token semantics, property tests that randomly interleave writes/handoffs/demotes, and an integration replay with deterministic RNG where we validate invariants. also add a regression that simulates low-signal micro-tenants to confirm we don't thrash origin.

hafsa: agreed. quick log example from prototype run (sanitized):

hafsa: ```
[2026-06-08T14:02:11Z] demote_eval: prefix=cfg:X123 tenant=team-g prob=0.42 draw=0.17 -> demote (token_seq=842 stable_until=2026-06-08T14:03:05Z)
[2026-06-08T14:02:12Z] rehydrate_lru: hit prefix=cfg:X123 tenant=team-g served_from=local_rehydrate latency=4ms
[2026-06-08T14:02:12Z] write: prefix=cfg:X123 tenant=team-g last_write=2026-06-08T14:02:12.345Z -> write_pin set
[2026-06-08T14:02:13Z] demote_blocked: prefix=cfg:X123 reason=recent_write
```

colin: numbers? cost vs risk?

hafsa: small canary (6 multi-tenant hosts, 6h): token egress down 8.7%, rehydrate_lru_hit_rate ~ 0.6 for demoted prefixes, origin-reads for affected micro-tenants +2.1% peak but stabilized after adjusting write_pin_ttl from 30s -> 60s. tail-read latency increase limited to +12ms p99 for those tenants.

grace: good. ops metrics to add before rollout?

hafsa: yes: evict_attempt_total, evict_allowed_by_token, evict_blocked_no_token, evict_blocked_recent_write, rehydrate_lru_hit, tenant_eviction_budget_utilization. add an alert: if tenant_eviction_budget_utilization > 90% for >10m AND origin_reads increase > 5% rollback.

mike: deployment plan?

hafsa: canary 1% multi-tenant hosts for 24h; exclude Dedicated. stage flags: enable_token_check, rehydrate_lru_size, write_pin_ttl, tenant_budget_map. will ramp based on rehydrate_lru_hit and evict_blocked_no_token trends.

deploy-bot: canary plan scheduled -> group=ownership-token-rehydrate-canary hosts=otrc-canary-1..otrc-canary-6 start=2026-06-09T02:00:00Z

colin: last item: doc the invariant prominently in the repo and tie unit tests to it: \"Evict allowed iff (ownership_token.valid && token.age_ms >= min_age && now - last_write_ms > write_pin_ttl && tenant_budget_allows)\". also note where ownership service must guarantee stable_until semantics.

hafsa: will add invariant, unit tests, and a small explainer in the runtime README. opening PR with flags + metrics + test plan now. please comment on the PR if you see edge cases.
